mainTopic: The special status of ארץ ישראל and the sources of rain; when to begin asking for rain; and the first fasts when rain is late
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer from the previous daf: a פסוק about water rising from the earth describes only בריאת העולם. A ברייתא then lists ways ארץ ישראל is special. It was created first, ה׳ waters it Himself, it gets real rain while the rest of the world gets the leftovers, and it drinks first. The גמרא finds a source in a one-letter difference between two פסוקים for רבי אליעזר's claim that ocean water is sweetened in the clouds. It then shows how רבי יהושע reads those פסוקים and matches a ברייתא about the upper waters to his view. Further teachings say the whole world drinks from the runoff of גן עדן, compare the sizes of the world, עדן and גיהנם, and praise בבל for being watered by its rivers. A new משנה sets when we begin asking for rain: the third of מרחשון, or the seventh according to רבן גמליאל, whom the halacha follows. Outside ארץ ישראל we start sixty days into the autumn season, counting day sixty itself. The next משנה teaches that if no rain falls, first the רבנן and then the whole community take on light fasts, held on Monday, Thursday and Monday.

steps.title: The earlier verse speaks about the creation of the world
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of an answer from the previous daf: the פסוק under discussion describes the time of בריאת העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is talking about the creation of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous daf. It says the פסוק being discussed is about how things were when the world was first created.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous daf, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argued about where the world's water comes from: the ocean or the upper waters. A פסוק about water rising from the earth seemed to support the ocean view. This answer, given for רבי יהושע, limits that פסוק to the time of בריאת העולם, so it does not describe how rain works today.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the tail end of a discussion that started on the previous daf, so do not read it as the start of the ברייתא that follows.

phrases.english: [That verse speaks] about the creation of the world.
phrases.notes: This line finishes a sentence that began on the previous daf, so the words in brackets just fill in how that sentence started.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun on the previous daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the verse to a specific time period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might describe how the world gets water today.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes the time of בריאת העולם only.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל was created before the rest of the world
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ארץ ישראל was created first and the rest of the world afterward, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: ארץ ישראל was created first and the rest of the world afterward, as the פסוק says, 'While He had not yet made the land and the outside places.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that begins listing the special qualities of ארץ ישראל. The first point is that it was created before everywhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions 'ארץ' (the land) first and 'חוצות' (the outside places) second. The ברייתא reads 'ארץ' as ארץ ישראל and 'חוצות' as the rest of the world, so the order of the words shows the order of creation.

keyTerms.meaning: The land. Here it means ארץ ישראל.
The outside places. Here it means the rest of the world.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The Land of Israel was created first
and the whole rest of the world was created afterward,
as it says: 'While He had not yet made the land and the outside places.'
phrases.notes: משלי 8:26. 'Land' means ארץ ישראל and 'outside places' means everywhere else, all through this ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל נִבְרֵאת תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about ארץ ישראל, connected to the topic of rain and creation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל was created before the rest of the world.

steps.title: ה׳ waters ארץ ישראל Himself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: הקדוש ברוך הוא waters ארץ ישראל directly, while the rest of the world is watered through a messenger.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself waters ארץ ישראל, while the rest of the world is watered through a messenger, as it says, 'Who gives rain upon the land, and sends water upon the outside places.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second special quality of ארץ ישראל‎: ה׳ waters it directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק‎, ה׳ 'gives' (נותן) rain on the land Himself, but He 'sends' (שולח) water to the outside places. Sending suggests a messenger, so the rest of the world gets its water less directly.

phrases.english: The Land of Israel is watered
by the Holy One, Blessed be He, Himself,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִיחַ,
phrases.english: and the whole rest of the world through a messenger,
as it says: 'Who gives rain upon the land'
'and sends water upon the outside places.'
phrases.notes: איוב 5:10

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַשְׁקֶה אוֹתָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second special quality of ארץ ישראל in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ waters ארץ ישראל directly and the rest of the world through a messenger.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל gets real rain; the world gets the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: ארץ ישראל drinks actual rainwater, while the rest of the world drinks the leftover residue.
steps.simpleTranslation: ארץ ישראל drinks rainwater, and the rest of the world drinks from what is left over, as it says, 'Who gives rain upon the land,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third special quality. ארץ ישראל gets the real rain, and the rest of the world gets only the leftover water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק is read in a new way. The land receives 'מטר', real rain. Then the remaining water, the leftovers, is sent to the outside places.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on. The rest of the פסוק is assumed.

phrases.english: The Land of Israel drinks rainwater,
and the whole rest of the world drinks from the leftover residue,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הַנֹּתֵן מָטָר עַל פְּנֵי אָרֶץ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'Who gives rain upon the land, etc.'
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the end of the same פסוק: 'and sends water upon the outside places.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוֹתָה מֵי גְשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק to teach a third quality.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל gets true rainwater and the rest of the world gets the residue.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל drinks first, explained with a cheese parable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: ארץ ישראל drinks first and the rest of the world afterward, like a cheese-maker who keeps the good part and leaves the waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: ארץ ישראל drinks first and the rest of the world afterward, as it says, 'Who gives rain upon the land,' and so on. It is like a person making cheese: he takes the food and leaves the waste.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a fourth special quality, that ארץ ישראל gets its water first. It explains this with a משל about making cheese.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the פסוק, land first and outside places second, shows the order of watering. In the משל, the cheese-maker first takes out the good food and leaves the waste behind. In the same way, ארץ ישראל is served first and gets the best.

keyTerms.meaning: Waste, the leftover part that is not used

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives four special qualities of ארץ ישראל: (1) it was created first, (2) ה׳ waters it Himself, (3) it gets real rain while the world gets leftovers, and (4) it drinks first. All of them come from reading 'ארץ' as ארץ ישראל and 'חוצות' as the rest of the world.

phrases.english: The Land of Israel drinks first,
and the whole rest of the world afterward,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הַנֹּתֵן מָטָר עַל פְּנֵי אָרֶץ וְגוֹ׳״ —
phrases.english: as it says: 'Who gives rain upon the land, etc.'
It is like a person who kneads cheese:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹטֵל אֶת הָאוֹכֵל וּמַנִּיחַ אֶת הַפְּסוֹלֶת.
phrases.english: he takes the food and leaves the waste.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוֹתָה תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final quality in the ברייתא and illustrates it with a משל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל is watered before the rest of the world.

steps.title: What is the source that ocean water becomes sweet in the clouds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes an earlier statement that salty ocean water is sweetened in the clouds and asks where this idea comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said above: they are sweetened in the clouds. Where does he learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier statement, that ocean water turns sweet inside the clouds. It asks for the source, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, someone asked how the world could drink ocean water, since it is salty. The answer was that it becomes sweet in the clouds. Now the גמרא wants to know what פסוק supports that claim.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know this?

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the previous daf, where salty ocean water was said to turn sweet in the clouds.

phrases.english: They are sweetened in the clouds.
From where does he know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מִמַּתְּקִין הֵן בְּעָבִים. מְנָלֵיהּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and returns to a claim from the earlier discussion about ocean water.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the claim that ocean water becomes sweet in the clouds.

steps.title: Two nearly identical verses show the source
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף, quoting רבי יוחנן, points to two פסוקים that are almost the same: one says 'חשכת מים' and the other 'חשרת מים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one פסוק says 'Darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies,' and another says 'Gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by bringing two פסוקים that differ by only one word. The next step explains what that difference teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים match except for one letter: 'חשכת' in one and 'חשרת' in the other. רבי יוחנן will use that small change to show that the water in the clouds changes and becomes sweet.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not finished here. So far רבי יוחנן has only placed the two פסוקים side by side. The next step explains what the one-letter difference teaches.

phrases.english: For Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is written: 'Darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 18:12

phrases.english: and it is written: 'Gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 22:12. Notice that only one letter changes, כ to ר.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source lies in the difference between two nearly identical פסוקים, 'חשכת מים' and 'חשרת מים'. Step 8 completes the explanation.

steps.title: Combining the two spellings into one word
steps.stepSummary: Take the כ from 'חשכת' and the ר from 'חשרת' to read 'חכשרת', meaning that the water is made fit in the clouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take the letter כ, put it together with the ר, and read it as 'חכשרת', meaning making fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 7. It shows how the two almost-matching פסוקים combine into one new word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים differ by only one letter, כ versus ר. Putting both letters together produces 'חכשרת', which means 'making fit'. So the פסוק hints that the clouds make salty ocean water fit to drink, which is the source step 6 asked for.
steps.whatToRemember: The source that ocean water is sweetened in the clouds is the word 'חכשרת', which comes from combining 'חשכת' and 'חשרת'.

phrases.english: Take the letter kaf
phrases.notes: This is the כ from 'חשכת' in the first פסוק.

phrases.english: and put it with the reish
phrases.notes: This is the ר from 'חשרת' in the second פסוק.

phrases.english: and read it as "chakhsharat" (making fit).

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁקוֹל כָּף וּשְׁדִי אַרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 7 by showing how the two spellings combine.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The combined word 'חכשרת' shows that water is made fit (sweetened) in the clouds.

steps.title: What does רבי יהושע learn from these verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהושע does with these two פסוקים, since they were just used to support the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע, what does he learn from these פסוקים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יהושע reads the two פסוקים. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים were just used to support the idea that ocean water is sweetened in the clouds. רבי יהושע holds that the world's rain comes from the upper waters, not the ocean. So the גמרא wants to know what he learns from these פסוקים instead.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he learn from them?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua, regarding these verses,
what does he learn from them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, בְּהָנֵי קְרָאֵי מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the reading that supports one view to ask how the other view reads the same פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יהושע explains the פסוקים of 'חשכת מים' and 'חשרת מים'.

steps.title: Dark clouds hold much water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע agrees with a saying from ארץ ישראל: bright clouds have little water, and dark clouds have much water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like what רב דימי said when he came from ארץ ישראל: they say there, 'Bright clouds have little water; dark clouds have much water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע uses the פסוקים to teach that dark clouds carry a lot of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, 'darkness of waters' (חשכת) and 'gathering of waters' (חשרת) go together. When clouds are dark, a lot of water is gathered in them. So the פסוקים describe how clouds look when they are full, and they say nothing about sweetening ocean water.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: He holds like this teaching,
that when Rav Dimi came, he said:
They say in the West:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: Bright clouds have little water.
Dark clouds have much water.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כִּי הָא דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע reads the פסוקים as teaching that dark clouds are full of water.

steps.title: Whose view fits the teaching about the upper waters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying the upper waters hang by God's word and their 'fruit' is rain, and asks whose view it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow: 'The upper waters hang by God's word, and their fruit is rainwater, as it says, "The earth is filled from the fruit of Your works"'? Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about the upper waters and asks which side of the dispute it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that rain is the 'fruit' of the upper waters. That ties the world's rain to water from above. The גמרא wants to pin down which of the two תנאים holds this way.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which was taught:
The upper waters
are hanging by the word of God,
and their fruit is rainwater,
as it says: "From the fruit of Your works
phrases.notes: תהלים 104:13

phrases.english: the earth is satisfied."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from reading the פסוקים to identifying which view a ברייתא follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the ברייתא about the upper waters follows.

steps.title: The teaching follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יהושע, who holds that rain comes from the upper waters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? רבי יהושע's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא matches רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע holds that the world drinks from the upper waters. A ברייתא calling rain the 'fruit' of the upper waters fits his view directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the view of רבי יהושע

phrases.english: Whose view? Rabbi Yehoshua's.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.

steps.title: How רבי אליעזר reads that verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains that the פסוק 'From the fruit of Your works' is about God's handiwork, not about the upper waters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? That פסוק is written about the work of God's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי אליעזר deals with the פסוק used in the ברייתא. It shows he reads the פסוק a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא read 'Your works' as the upper waters. רבי אליעזר reads 'Your works' simply as everything God made, so the פסוק gives no proof about where rain comes from. This way his own view stays standing.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what it is written about

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the upper waters fits רבי יהושע, and רבי אליעזר reads its פסוק as being about God's handiwork in general.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer would say:
That verse is about the work of the hands
of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
that is what it is written about.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הָהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the other view after the ברייתא was matched to רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק 'From the fruit of Your works' proves that rain comes from the upper waters, against רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק as being about God's handiwork in general, so it proves nothing about the source of rain.

steps.title: The whole world drinks from the runoff of גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that the entire world drinks from the leftover runoff of גן עדן, based on 'A river goes out from Eden'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The whole world drinks from the runoff of גן עדן, as it says, 'And a river goes out from Eden.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי יהושע בן לוי says the whole world gets its water from what is left over after גן עדן is watered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a river goes out of Eden to water the garden. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns that the garden is watered first, and whatever flows on beyond it waters the rest of the world. This matches the idea from step 5 that the more important place drinks first and the rest gets what is left.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The entire world
drinks from the runoff of the Garden of Eden,
as it says: "And a river goes out of Eden, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:10. The 'etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק, 'to water the garden.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new teaching on the theme of where the world's water comes from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole world drinks from the leftover runoff of גן עדן.

steps.title: A big field's runoff waters a small field
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the runoff of a בית כור waters an area the size of a תרקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: The runoff of a בית כור waters a תרקב.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a comparison to the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי. The runoff from a large field is enough to water only a much smaller field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית כור is a large field, and a תרקב is a much smaller piece of land. Placed right after the teaching about גן עדן, the comparison suggests that גן עדן is far bigger than the rest of the world, which lives off its runoff.

keyTerms.meaning: A large field, big enough to sow a כור of seed
A small field, big enough to sow half a סאה of seed

steps.whatToRemember: The world lives on the leftover water of גן עדן, the way a small field can live on the runoff of a much bigger one.

phrases.english: It was taught: From the runoff of a beit kor
phrases.notes: A בית כור is a big field, enough land to sow a כור of seed.

phrases.english: a tarkav is watered.
phrases.notes: A תרקב is a much smaller field, enough land to sow half a סאה of seed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: מִתַּמְצִית בֵּית כּוֹר שׁוֹתֶה תַּרְקַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a size comparison to the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי about the runoff of גן עדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The runoff of a בית כור is enough to water a תרקב.

steps.title: Comparing the sizes of מצרים, the world, the גן, עדן and גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a chain of size comparisons. Each place is one sixtieth of the next, all the way from מצרים up to גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: מצרים is 400 by 400 פרסה. מצרים is one sixtieth of כוש, כוש is one sixtieth of the world, the world is one sixtieth of the גן, the גן is one sixtieth of עדן, and עדן is one sixtieth of גיהנם. So the whole world is like a little pot lid sitting on top of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that measures the world by comparing it to bigger and bigger places. It continues the theme of the last steps about עדן and the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step said the world drinks from the leftover water of גן עדן. This ברייתא shows how huge the גן and עדן are compared to our world. Each step in the chain multiplies the size by sixty, so גיהנם turns out to be enormous.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of distance, a few miles long
Cush, a large land south of Egypt
Eden itself, the larger area the Garden is part of
Gehenna, the place where the wicked are punished

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The land of Egypt is

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה עַל אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה,
phrases.english: four hundred parasangs by four hundred parasangs,
phrases.notes: A פרסה is a distance of a few miles, so this is a big square of land.

phrases.english: and it is one sixtieth of Cush,
and Cush is one sixtieth of the world,
and the world is one sixtieth of the Garden,
and the Garden is one sixtieth of Eden,
and Eden is one sixtieth of Gehenna.
It turns out that the entire world
is like a pot lid for Gehenna.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הָוְיָא אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת פַּרְסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the aggadic theme of עדן and the world's water by giving size comparisons
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each place in the chain is one sixtieth of the next, so the whole world is like a pot lid compared to גיהנם.

steps.title: Other opinions: גיהנם or עדן has no measure
steps.stepSummary: Two other views say the sizes cannot be measured at all. One says גיהנם has no limit, and another says עדן has no limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: גיהנם has no measure. And some say: עדן has no measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds two other opinions that disagree with the exact numbers just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view gave every place a set size. These views say one of the places is too big to measure. One says it is גיהנם, and the other says it is עדן.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: גֵּיהִנָּם אֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר,
phrases.english: And some say: Gehenna has no measure.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: עֵדֶן אֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר.
phrases.english: And some say: Eden has no measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: גֵּיהִנָּם אֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers other opinions that reject the fixed size given for גיהנם or עדן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some hold that גיהנם has no limit, and some hold that עדן has no limit.

steps.title: בבל's storehouses are full because it sits on many waters
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains a פסוק in ירמיהו: בבל is full of grain because it lies on great rivers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: What does the פסוק 'You who dwell on many waters, rich in storehouses' mean? What made בבל's storehouses full of grain? You must say it is because it sits on many waters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the subject of how lands get their water. רבי אושעיא shows that בבל's food comes from its rivers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was rain and runoff. Here we learn that a land can be rich without rain if it has rivers to water its fields. The פסוק links בבל's 'many waters' to its 'many storehouses.'

keyTerms.meaning: You must say, meaning this is the only answer

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"You who dwell on many waters, rich in storehouses"?
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 51:13, said about בבל.

phrases.english: What caused Babylonia
to have its storehouses full of grain?
You must say:
because it dwells on many waters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the size of the world to how a particular land, בבל, gets its water
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל's storehouses are full because it sits on rivers.

steps.title: בבל is rich because it harvests without rain
steps.stepSummary: רב says בבל is wealthy because its crops grow even without rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: בבל is rich, because it harvests crops without rain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a short statement that supports רבי אושעיא's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא explained the reason, which is the rivers. רב states the result: בבל does not depend on rain to have a harvest, and that makes it rich.

phrases.english: Rav said:
Babylonia is rich,
since it harvests without rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: עַתִּירָה בָּבֶל דְּחָצְדָא בְּלָא מִיטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אושעיא's point about בבל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל can harvest without rain, and that is why it is rich.

steps.title: Better a swampy land than a dry one
steps.stepSummary: אביי says we have a tradition that a wet, swampy land is better than a dry one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition: better swampy than dry.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes the discussion about בבל with a general rule about land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא and רב praised בבל's rivers. אביי turns this into a general rule: too much water is better for a land than too little.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: בבל does not depend on rain because its rivers water the land. That is why a wet land is considered better than a dry one.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition:
swampy, and not dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נְקִיטִינַן, טוֹבְעָנִי וְלֹא יוֹבְשָׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the praise of בבל into a general rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A swampy land is better than a dry one.

steps.title: New משנה: start asking for rain on the third of מרחשון
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that we begin asking for rain in the עמידה on the third of מרחשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: On the third of מרחשון we begin asking for rain.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us the date when we start adding the request for rain in davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a practical rule. It is not about mentioning rain, but about actually asking for it in ברכת השנים. The first opinion sets the date as the third of מרחשון.

keyTerms.meaning: We ask for rain, by adding 'ותן טל ומטר' in the עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: Asking for rain (שאלה, 'ותן טל ומטר') is different from mentioning rain ('משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם'). This משנה is only about asking.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
On the third of Marcheshvan
we request the rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה בִּמְרַחְשְׁוָן שׁוֹאֲלִין אֶת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new halachic topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We begin asking for rain on the third of מרחשון.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: wait until the seventh so the last pilgrim gets home
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says to start on the seventh of מרחשון, fifteen days after סוכות, so the farthest pilgrim can reach the נהר פרת before the rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: on the seventh of the month, fifteen days after the חג, so that the last Jew can reach the Euphrates River.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל disagrees with the first opinion and gives a later date, along with his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pilgrims walked home from ירושלים after סוכות. Those living far away, near the נהר פרת, needed fifteen days. רבן גמליאל does not want us asking for rain that would bother them on the road.

keyTerms.meaning: The last Jew, the pilgrim with the longest trip home

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says: On the seventh of it,
phrases.notes: 'Of it' means of מרחשון.

phrases.english: fifteen days after the Festival,
so that the last of the Jewish people can reach
the Euphrates River.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: בְּשִׁבְעָה בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion and gives a later date
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Start asking for rain on the seventh of מרחשון, so pilgrims can travel home dry.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר rules like רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבי אלעזר's ruling that the halacha follows רבן גמליאל, so we start on the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אלעזר said: The halacha is like רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by deciding which opinion is the halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had two dates, the third and the seventh. רבי אלעזר decides that we follow the later date of רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Elazar said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions in the משנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In ארץ ישראל we begin asking for rain on the seventh of מרחשון.

steps.title: חנניה: outside ארץ ישראל, wait until sixty days into the season
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes חנניה: in the גולה we start asking for rain sixty days after the start of the autumn season.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: חנניה says: And in the גולה, we wait until sixty days into the תקופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different rule for Jews living outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's dates were for ארץ ישראל. חנניה says the גולה, meaning בבל, follows a later schedule. It is counted by the solar season, sixty days after the תקופה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: A solar season; here the autumn season that starts at the equinox

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice outside ארץ ישראל of starting 'ותן טל ומטר' in early December, not in מרחשון.

phrases.english: It was taught: Chananya says:
And in the Diaspora, not until sixty days into the season.
phrases.notes: He means sixty days after the autumn season starts, at the equinox.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, חֲנַנְיָה אוֹמֵר: וּבַגּוֹלָה, עַד שִׁשִּׁים בַּתְּקוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate rule for Jews outside ארץ ישראל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the גולה, we begin asking for rain sixty days into the autumn season.

steps.title: שמואל rules like חנניה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא quotes שמואל: the halacha follows חנניה for the גולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said in the name of שמואל: The halacha is like חנניה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms that חנניה's rule for the גולה is the halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two rulings. In ארץ ישראל we follow רבן גמליאל and start on the seventh of מרחשון. In the גולה we follow חנניה and start sixty days into the תקופה.
steps.whatToRemember: In ארץ ישראל we start asking for rain on the seventh of מרחשון, like רבן גמליאל. In the גולה we start sixty days after the autumn תקופה, like חנניה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chiyya said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is in accordance with Chananya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כַּחֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules that חנניה's view is the halacha
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Outside ארץ ישראל, we begin asking for rain sixty days into the autumn season.

steps.title: Challenge: שמואל gave a different sign for starting to ask for rain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל could rule like חנניה (sixty days) when he himself named a different marker: when wood is brought into the house of טבות the bird hunter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't they ask שמואל, 'From when do we say "ותן טל ומטר"?' He answered: 'From when they bring wood into the house of טבות the bird hunter!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 25. שמואל seems to have given a different starting point than the sixty days of חנניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25, שמואל ruled like חנניה: start sixty days after the autumn season begins. Here, when asked directly, שמואל gave a local event as the starting point instead. That looks like a different date, so his two statements seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely... (brings a source that seems to contradict)
'And give dew and rain', the request for rain in the עמידה

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But they asked Shmuel:
From when do we mention "And give dew and rain"?
He said to them: From when they bring wood
into the house of Tavut the bird hunter!
phrases.notes: שמואל is pointing to a familiar local event as his sign, not giving a number of days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מִשְּׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in step 25 using another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the halacha follows חנניה's sixty days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל elsewhere named a different marker (wood brought to טבות's house), which seems to be a different date than sixty days.

steps.title: Answer: both signs are the same time
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the wood-bringing sign and the sixty days are one and the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this one and that one are the same amount of time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: there is no clash, because both markers land on the same date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wood being brought in happens around sixty days into the season. So שמואל was just giving a practical sign for the same date as חנניה. His two statements agree.

phrases.english: Perhaps this and that
are one measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי חַד שִׁיעוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: the two markers are the same time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's wood-sign seemed to be a different date than sixty days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wood-sign is just a practical marker for the sixtieth day, so שמואל agrees with חנניה.

steps.title: Does day sixty itself count as before or after?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask whether the sixtieth day belongs to the period before sixty or after sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is the sixtieth day treated like the days before sixty, or like the days after sixty?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the count is sixty days, the גמרא asks a precise question about the edge: does day sixty itself count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If day sixty counts as 'after,' we start asking for rain on day sixty. If it counts as 'before,' we start only on day sixty-one. This sets up the next step, which brings an answer.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Is the sixtieth day like before sixty
or like after sixty?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים, כְּלִפְנֵי שִׁשִּׁים אוֹ כִּלְאַחַר שִׁשִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up detail about חנניה's sixty-day count.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the sixtieth day counts as part of the period before or after sixty.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about day sixty
steps.stepSummary: רב says day sixty counts as after sixty, and שמואל says it counts as before sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב said, the sixtieth day is like after sixty. שמואל said, the sixtieth day is like before sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that it is a dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, we start asking for rain on day sixty itself. According to שמואל, we wait until day sixty-one. Here the question is shown to be an argument, and step 31 gives the final ruling.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rav said:
The sixtieth day is like after sixty,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים כְּלִפְנֵי שִׁשִּׁים.
phrases.english: and Shmuel said: The sixtieth day is like before sixty.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, רַב אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 by presenting a dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a מחלוקת: רב counts day sixty as after (start on day sixty), שמואל counts it as before (start on day sixty-one).

steps.title: A memory aid for who holds what
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a sign to remember the dispute: those above need water, those below do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Your memory aid is, 'Those above need water; those below don't need water.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a memory trick so we don't mix up which of רב or שמואל said which opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one from the higher place, who needs rain more, starts asking earlier, on day sixty. That is רב. The one from the lower place, which gets water flowing down to it, starts later. That is שמואל.
steps.confusionAlert: This is only a memory aid, not a reason or proof for either opinion.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
And your mnemonic: those above need water,
phrases.notes: 'Those above' is רב, who learned in high ארץ ישראל, so he starts asking earlier.

phrases.english: those below do not need water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסִימָנָךְ עִלָּאֵי בָּעוּ מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a memory aid for the dispute in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remember: the higher place (רב) starts earlier; the lower place (שמואל) starts later.

steps.title: Halacha: day sixty counts as after sixty
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that the halacha follows רב: day sixty counts as after sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The halacha is that the sixtieth day is like after sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the dispute and rules like רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since day sixty counts as 'after,' in the גולה we begin saying ותן טל ומטר on day sixty itself. This closes the topic of when to start asking for rain.
steps.whatToRemember: In ארץ ישראל we start asking for rain on the seventh of מרחשון (like רבן גמליאל). In the גולה we start sixty days after the autumn season begins (like חנניה), counting day sixty itself (like רב).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The halakha is:
The sixtieth day is like after sixty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute of step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows רב: in the גולה we begin asking for rain on the sixtieth day.

steps.title: משנה: individuals fast if no rain by the seventeenth of מרחשון
steps.stepSummary: If the seventeenth of מרחשון comes with no rain, individuals start three fasts. These are light fasts: eating at night is allowed, and work, washing, oil, shoes and marital relations are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seventeenth of מרחשון arrived and no rain fell, the individuals begin to fast three fasts. They eat and drink after dark, and are allowed to work, wash, smear oil, wear shoes, and have marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the first stage of response when rain is late: certain individuals take on three light fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only individuals fast at this stage, not the whole community. The fasts are mild: they run only from morning, so eating at night is fine, and none of the other restrictions of a severe fast apply.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If the seventeenth of Marḥeshvan arrived
and rain has not fallen —
the individuals begin to fast
three fasts.
They eat and drink after dark,
and they are permitted in work and in bathing
and in smearing oil and in wearing shoes
and in marital relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הִגִּיעַ שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּמַרְחֶשְׁוָן וְלֹא יָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה about what to do when rain does not come.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No rain by 17 מרחשון: individuals take on three light fasts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first rung of a ladder of fasts that gets stricter the longer rain is withheld.

steps.title: משנה: בית דין decrees community fasts by ראש חודש כסלו
steps.stepSummary: If ראש חודש כסלו comes and still no rain, בית דין decrees three fasts on the whole community, with the same light rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: If ראש חודש כסלו arrived and no rain fell, בית דין decrees three fasts on the community. They eat and drink after dark, and are allowed to work, wash, smear oil, wear shoes, and have marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the second stage: now the whole community fasts, by order of בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What changes is who fasts and who decides: the whole צבור instead of individuals, and it is ordered by בית דין. The rules of the fast stay the same light ones as before.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though the whole community now fasts, these fasts are still light ones. Only the stage and who fasts have changed.

phrases.english: If the New Moon of Kislev arrived
and rain has not fallen —
the court decrees three fasts
on the community.
They eat and drink after dark,
and they are permitted in work and in bathing
and in smearing oil and in wearing shoes
and in marital relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעַ רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ כִּסְלֵיו וְלֹא יָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the next, broader stage of fasting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No rain by ראש חודש כסלו: בית דין decrees three light fasts on the whole community.

steps.title: Who are the individuals in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking who the 'individuals' who fast first are.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who are the 'individuals' that the משנה mentions?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section begins. It asks who the 'individuals' are, the ones the משנה says start fasting on the seventeenth of מרחשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said יחידים fast before the whole community does, but it never said who they are. Is it any private person, or a special group? The גמרא wants a clear definition.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Individuals; here, the special people who fast before the community

phrases.english: Gemara:
Who are the "individuals"?
phrases.notes: This is the word from the משנה about the seventeenth of מרחשון (step 32).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן ״יְחִידִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's term יחידים from step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the 'individuals' who fast first.

steps.title: רב הונא: the individuals are the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the 'individuals' are the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: they are the רבנן (the Torah scholars).
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. The 'individuals' are the רבנן, the Torah scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So יחידים does not mean any private person who chooses to fast. It means the scholars, who are the first to take on fasts when rain is late.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.

steps.title: The individuals' three fasts are Monday, Thursday, Monday
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא adds that the individuals' three fasts fall on Monday, Thursday and Monday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: the individuals fast three fasts, on Monday, Thursday, and Monday.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא makes a second statement. He sets the days of the week for the individuals' three fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'three fasts' and did not say which days. רב הונא fills this in: the fasts follow a set order, starting on a Monday, then the next Thursday, then the following Monday.

keyTerms.meaning: Monday, Thursday and Monday (literally the second, fifth and second days of the week)

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:
Individuals fast three fasts,
Monday, Thursday, and Monday.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר רַב הוּנָא: יְחִידִים מִתְעַנִּין שָׁלֹשׁ תַּעֲנִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement from רב הונא about the same individuals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Individuals' three fasts are Monday, Thursday, Monday.

steps.title: Why say it? A משנה already teaches this order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב הונא adds, since a משנה already says the first three fasts are Monday, Thursday, Monday.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in a משנה: a fast is not decreed on the community starting on a Thursday, so prices will not shoot up. Rather, the first three fasts are Monday, Thursday, and Monday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. His rule seems to repeat what a משנה already says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה already says the first three fasts go Monday, Thursday, Monday, and never start on a Thursday. If that is already known, רב הונא's statement seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asks what a statement adds)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
We do not decree a fast on the community
starting on a Thursday,
so as not to make the prices jump,
rather, the first three fasts
are Monday, Thursday, and Monday!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָמַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's statement in step 36 as already known.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that individuals fast Monday, Thursday, Monday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same order is already stated in a משנה, so his statement seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Without רב הונא, we might think individuals are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה spoke only about a community. Without רב הונא, we might think an individual does not need this order.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: that rule applies only to a community, but not to an individual. So רב הונא teaches us that it applies to individuals too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains what new point רב הונא teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה talks about the צבור. We might have thought the Monday-Thursday-Monday order is only for a community fast. רב הונא teaches that individuals follow the same order.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken assumption)

phrases.english: You might have said:
this applies to a community,
but to an individual, no,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement adds a new case (individuals) not covered by the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Monday-Thursday-Monday order applies only to a community fast.
steps.terutzMaskana: Individuals must also follow the Monday-Thursday-Monday order.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also teaches that individuals fast Monday, Thursday, Monday, and that they stop for ראשי חודשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: when the individuals start to fast, they fast Monday, Thursday, and Monday, and they stop for ראשי חודשים...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב הונא. The ברייתא keeps going past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא clearly says that individuals use the Monday-Thursday-Monday order, just like רב הונא. It adds that if a fast day lands on ראש חודש, they stop and do not fast on that day.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught so in a ברייתא (support)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'individuals' are the רבנן. Their three fasts are Monday, Thursday, Monday, the same order as a community fast, and a ברייתא backs this up.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
When the individuals begin to fast,
they fast Monday, Thursday, and Monday,
and they stop for New Moons,

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a ברייתא for רב הונא's rule as explained in step 38.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that individuals fast Monday, Thursday, Monday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that individuals fast Monday, Thursday, Monday and stop for ראשי חודשים.
